transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-07-11
Time: 09:00 - 09:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (BlueMesa Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (BlueMesa VP Eng), Diego Suarez (BlueMesa Cloud Ops)

---
Summary (auto):
- BlueMesa is preparing for a summer product launch that increases inference traffic ~3-4x during certain windows.
- Team wants a predictable SLO for 99th percentile latency, and tighter cost controls for nightly batch runs.
- Decision leaning toward a dedicated pilot but wants clear fallback to hosted and proof points on tail latency and encryption/KMS.

---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know it's early east coast so appreciate the time. Very quick agenda — health check, cost trends last quarter, capacity ask for launch, and then a handoff to Raj and Lena for pilot.
[00:16] Aisha Khan: Hey Maya, thanks. We are tight on time but yes this is the one where we need to be really clear on the 99th pct tail.
[00:22] Tom Reynolds: Yeah, the launch is July 28 so we need a plan that doesn't, uh, surprise SRE.
[00:28] Raj Patel: Totally. We've looked at your telemetry but we wanted the canonical prompt set so we can run the same bench on dedicated infra.
[00:35] Diego Suarez: Right, and also firewall / VPC peering windows — we need to not break existing flows.
[00:41] Maya Chen: Understood. Quick call-out on spend: your last 90 days show a step-up during late-night batch runs. Lena, do you want to pull the numbers?
[00:52] Lena Ortiz: Sure — I'll keep it high-level, the token spend is up ~38% month over month for the transform jobs, and average latency is steady but the 95/99 tails drift when concurrent streaming sessions spike.
[01:08] Aisha Khan: That's the part we worry about — our users see long tails when we have simultaneous QA sessions and live inference. Any mitigations besides dialing concurrency?
[01:18] Raj Patel: There's batching and prefix/KV cache tuning. For your workload, turning on prefix cache for repeated user prompts trimmed token re-compute by about 20% in our simulations, but that helps throughput more than tail latency.
[01:31] Tom Reynolds: So batching lowers cost but could increase tail?
[01:35] Raj Patel: It depends — continuous batching with latency SLO caps ensures small requests get prioritized. We can size the batch window to be aggressive during batch-only windows, and smaller during live traffic.
[01:47] Diego Suarez: Can Redwood do a hybrid where live routes go to hosted nodes and heavy batch jobs go to dedicated?
[01:54] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing can send by policy — you can route by latency vs cost. We often recommend a dedicated GPU pool for steady high-throughput plus a hosted fallback for spillover.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: Ok, what about encryption? We need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for SOC2.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: We also need SSO/SAML for the console, RBAC mapping to our groups.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Got it — we have SOC 2 type II, and we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping, plus audit logs via the console. I'll share the security brief after the call; Lena will run the governance call for deeper details.
[02:33] Tom Reynolds: Good. Back to latency — can you commit to a 99th percentile SLO for the pilot?
[02:39] Raj Patel: We can target a measurable SLO for the pilot period; first step is running the customer's prompt set on a dedicated config to estimate tail. If we see outliers, we can tweak kernel selection, quantization, and KV cache.
[02:54] Aisha Khan: Kernel selection? Like you pick different optimized kernels based on sequence length?
[02:58] Raj Patel: Exactly. The serving runtime selects optimized kernels based on seq length distribution and hardware; sometimes swapping kernels reduces tail in specific cases.
[03:06] Diego Suarez: Any flakiness with quantized variants? We tried a Q4 build elsewhere and saw hallucination spikes.
[03:12] Raj Patel: There's always tradeoffs — certain quantization profiles slightly affect output quality for very long context tasks. We'll run quality regressions against your eval sets as part of the bench.
[03:23] Aisha Khan: OK good. So pilot scope: 6 weeks dedicated, run bench with our prompt set, measure 50/95/99 and token cost, then decide commit. Is that right?
[03:33] Maya Chen: Yes, that's the ask we heard. I'll send an outline of the commercial pilot with committed capacity and optional burst pricing.
[03:41] Tom Reynolds: Billing — how will unused reserved capacity be handled? Do we get credits?
[03:46] Lena Ortiz: Commercial can be flexible; for pilots we usually do a partial commit with clear overage rates, and we can structure credits into the term based on usage thresholds.
[03:55] Diego Suarez: Also, we need to simulate a failure scenario — what happens if a GPU node has a hot restart? What's the fallback?
[04:02] Raj Patel: Auto-fallback to compatible model variants and/or hosted region. There's policy-based routing and model variant fallbacks; in practice we route to compatible lower-latency variants if the dedicated pool degrades.
[04:13] Aisha Khan: Can you provide a runbook with those steps so our SRE can tie into on-call?
[04:18] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll produce an incident runbook and include escalation points.
[04:22] Tom Reynolds: Great. A few nitty-gritty items: network egress, data residency, and logs retention.
[04:29] Lena Ortiz: Data residency — we can pin region for dedicated capacity, and audit logs retention can be extended as an add-on.
[04:36] Diego Suarez: On the peering, we need a maintenance window for VPC peering — is there a recommended step-by-step?
[04:42] Raj Patel: We'll send a preflight checklist for VPC peering and firewall rules — Diego, that should cover your team.
[04:48] Aisha Khan: Perfect. Two quick questions from my side — one on model rollouts and one on eval regressions.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Sure, go ahead.
[04:54] Aisha Khan: Rollouts — can we do canary and auto-fallback to previous model if quality drops?
[04:58] Raj Patel: Yes, canary rollouts and automatic fallback are supported. You can configure rollback triggers tied to eval metrics and latency.
[05:06] Aisha Khan: Eval regressions — do you keep time-series of eval scores so we can detect slow degradations?
[05:11] Lena Ortiz: We do; Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets and will alert on drift. We'll share sample dashboards.
[05:19] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. Any competitor concerns for us we should be aware of?
[05:23] Maya Chen: We occasionally get compared to OpenAI hosted costs and Anthropic on quality—they're mentioned in procurement reviews. We focus on predictable economics and private deployment options.
[05:34] Diego Suarez: Ok, action items?
[05:36] Maya Chen: I'll recap after, but Raj will run the bench, Aisha will send the prompt set and logs, Diego will confirm peering windows, and Lena will schedule the SOC2/KMS governance call.
[05:47] Raj Patel: I'll need access to the prompt set and a small, anonymized sample of logs. If you prefer, we can share a script to sanitize them.
[05:55] Aisha Khan: We'll use your sanitizer script. We'll aim to get the artifacts to you by next week.
[06:00] Tom Reynolds: Thanks. I also want the commercial template so finance can review.
[06:05] Maya Chen: Yes — I'll send the pilot commercial and a quick note on overage handling.
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: I'll own the governance deep-dive and schedule it for the week after next.
[06:14] Diego Suarez: One last — latency SLA language needs to be clear about measurement windows and what counts as an exception.
[06:20] Maya Chen: We'll draft an SLO appendix.
[06:23] Aisha Khan: Great.
[06:25] [crosstalk]
[06:28] Maya Chen: Ok let's do a quick recap and close.

Recap:
- Pilot: 6-week dedicated capacity pilot. Redwood to provide pricing template and overage terms (Maya).
- Bench: Raj to run 99th percentile latency benchmark on BlueMesa prompt set; include quantized variant tests and quality regression (Raj).
- Artifacts: BlueMesa to provide peak logs and sample prompts; use Redwood sanitizer if needed (Aisha).
- Networking: Diego to confirm peering windows and firewall rules (Diego).
- Security: Lena to schedule SOC2/KMS audit deep-dive and share audit docs (Lena).

Close:
[07:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with an email with the pilot terms and the benchmark plan. Expect docs in 24-48 hours.
[07:10] Aisha Khan: Thanks all.
[07:12] Tom Reynolds: Thanks.
[07:14] Diego Suarez: Bye.
